facts: The paper is titled "Understanding and Improving Information Preservation in Prompt Compression for LLMs."
Weronika Łajewska is affiliated with the University of Stavanger.
The research addresses challenges related to information loss in prompt compression techniques.
Lluís Màrquez is associated with the Technical University of Catalonia (UPC).
Recent advancements in large language models have led to their application in various tasks.
New prompt compression techniques have been developed to balance input length reduction with performance retention.
Improvements of up to 23% in downstream performance were achieved through refined soft prompting.
The optimal trade-off between effectiveness and compression rate was found with soft prompting combined with sequence-level training.
Recent advancements in large language models (LLMs) have enabled their application to tasks requiring long-context input.
The proposed holistic evaluation framework considers downstream task performance, grounding to original text, and information preservation.
The hard-prompting method LLMLingua and the soft-prompting methods xRAG and PISCO were analyzed using the evaluation framework.
PISCO achieves the best balance between compression rate and effectiveness among the methods evaluated.
Prompt compression enhances the efficiency of large language models (LLMs) by creating smaller, approximate representations of prompts.
Hard prompting focuses on producing concise text versions while retaining key information.
Notable soft prompting approaches include AutoCompressors, Gisting, ICAE, 500xCompressor, and xRAG.
Evaluation of these methods typically involves downstream tasks such as classification and QA.
The framework proposes including generation tasks with longer contexts for evaluating prompt compression methods.
Key evaluation dimensions include downstream task performance, response grounding, and information preservation.
Metrics like BERTScore and Exact Match are utilized for performance evaluation.
Performance data shows relative drops in performance when context is removed from various models, including Mistral-7B.

The analysis evaluates four prompt compression methods using the Mistral-7B Instruct v0.2 model. PISCO employs two adapters for context compression and response generation. Performance assessments reveal significant performance drops (3% to 55%) with compression, particularly in complex tasks like HotpotQA. PISCO maintains higher semantic similarity and entity retention compared to xRAG.
The authors propose a new training approach for the xRAG model called xRAG w/ Sentence PT + FT.
The modified xRAG model shows significant performance gains in grounding and entity preservation.
A two-step pre-training method is introduced to improve the model's ability to handle information across multiple tokens.
PISCO achieves superior compression rates without performance loss in long-context scenarios.
Many methods, particularly xRAG, struggle to preserve detailed information.
Modifications to xRAG have shown to improve retention and performance.
PISCO's sequence-level distillation enhances grounding and information preservation.
A hybrid approach combining hard and soft prompting minimizes information loss during compression.
The paper evaluates the quality of prompt compression methods in long-context generation tasks.
The study identifies that many existing methods struggle to maintain detailed information in long-context scenarios.
The proposed improvements to the xRAG method resulted in a 23% increase in downstream task performance.
The code repository for this research is available at https://github.com/amazon-science/information-preservation-in-prompt-compression.
The study exclusively uses Mistral-7B as the target large language model.
The analysis is confined to English benchmarks.
The evaluation includes only one representative baseline from each category of prompt compression techniques.
Further exploration is warranted in long-form question-answering scenarios.
Training of the xRAG model was conducted on two compute instances with 8 NVIDIA A100 GPUs.
The training utilized a dataset of 1,128,075 samples, with 628,003 including context.
Evaluation datasets included HotpotQA, arXiv-summarization, QuAC, GSM8K, and TriviaQA.
Mistral-7B achieved the highest grounding scores in a comparative analysis with xRAG, PISCO, and LLMLingua.
